# kubernetes

kubectl, kind, krew, and k9s helpers: secret inspection, debug pods, throwaway kind clusters, and evicted-pod triage.

---

## `k8s_create_cluster_with_registry`

Create a kind cluster wired to a local image registry, using the upstream example script. The script is downloaded to a temp file, diffed against the copy you approved last time, and executed only after you confirm.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Runs a script downloaded from the internet. Shows it and prompts first.

**Usage**

```sh
k8s_create_cluster_with_registry
```

**Examples**

```sh
k8s_create_cluster_with_registry
```

**Requires** `curl`, `kind`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:354`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L354)

## `k8s_create_kind_cluster`

Create a kind cluster and record its name so k8s_delete_last_cluster can find it later.

**Usage**

```sh
k8s_create_kind_cluster [name]
```

**Examples**

```sh
k8s_create_kind_cluster
k8s_create_kind_cluster scratch
```

**Requires** `kind`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:317`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L317)

**See also** `k8s_delete_kind_cluster`

## `k8s_encode_secret`

Base64-encode a value for pasting into a Secret manifest. Emits one unwrapped line on macOS and Linux alike.

**Usage**

```sh
k8s_encode_secret <value>...
```

**Examples**

```sh
k8s_encode_secret hunter2
```

**Requires** `base64`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:134`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L134)

## `k8s_fetch_kubectl_aliases`

Download ahmetb/kubectl-aliases into the shellrc cache. Explicitly user-invoked: nothing is ever fetched while your shell starts. The cached file is sourced automatically on the next shell if non-empty.

**Usage**

```sh
k8s_fetch_kubectl_aliases
```

**Examples**

```sh
k8s_fetch_kubectl_aliases && k8s_load_kubectl_aliases
```

**Requires** `curl`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:70`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L70)

**See also** `k8s_load_kubectl_aliases`

## `k8s_install_krew`

Download the latest krew release for this OS and architecture, show you its checksum and contents, and install it only after you agree. Nothing is piped into a shell.

**Usage**

```sh

```

**Examples**

```sh
k8s_install_krew
```

**Requires** `curl`, `tar`

## `k8s_print_connections`

Run netstat in every pod matching $LABEL in $NAMESPACE, optionally filtered, and report the per-pod line count. Full output is kept in a private temp directory whose path is printed at the end.

**Usage**

```sh
k8s_print_connections [grep-pattern]...
```

**Examples**

```sh
NAMESPACE=production LABEL=app=web k8s_print_connections ESTABLISHED
```

**Requires** `kubectl`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:176`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L176)

## `k9s_install_themes`

Install the k9s skin collection into the k9s config directory. On macOS also links the config dir into ~/Library/Application Support/, which is where k9s looks.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Replaces any existing skins directory. Prompts when one is present.

**Usage**

```sh
k9s_install_themes
```

**Examples**

```sh
k9s_install_themes && k9s_set_theme solarized_dark
```

**Requires** `git`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/kubernetes.sh:444`](../../modules/common/kubernetes.sh#L444)

**See also** `k9s_set_theme`

---
